key_insight: InterPrior introduces a scalable generative prior that lets high-level intentions (e.g., affordances) drive physically coherent whole-body human–object interactions, allowing balance, contact, and manipulation to emerge rather than be explicitly planned.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between high-level task intentions and low-level physically plausible whole-body motions by scaling motor and physics priors so humanoid agents can compose and generalize loco‑manipulation skills across diverse contexts.
method: Learn a large-scale generative prior over whole-body dynamics and contact-conditioned motor behavior from interaction data (simulation and/or real).
Condition the generative controller on high-level affordances/intention inputs to produce contact-aware, balanced trajectories rather than hand-crafted motion plans.
Use compact latent or hierarchical representations to scale the prior for compositional control and generalization across objects, tasks, and environments.
impact: Enables researchers and practitioners to build humanoid controllers that require less explicit motion engineering, generalize better to new objects and contexts, and produce physically plausible interactions—accelerating development of robust embodied agents and robot manipulation systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: intention/affordance → InterPrior (latent prior) → physics-based renderer/simulator → whole-body motion
Before/after gallery: explicit planned motions vs. InterPrior emergent contact-rich interactions
Contact & balance visualization: heatmaps or force vectors showing emergent contact points and center-of-mass stability over time
Scaling chart: performance/generalization vs. prior model size or dataset scale (illustrating improved compositionality)
paper_title: InterPrior: Scaling Generative Control for Physics-Based Human-Object Interactions
paper_authors: Sirui Xu, Samuel Schulter, Morteza Ziyadi, Xialin He, Xiaohan Fei
